text:
chen: Heads-up — seeing steady memory creep in the KV cache on the Dedicated pool after ~48h of long-context load. Paging and slab fragmentation spikes around 45–50s of sequence depth. cc @alice @diego

alice: ugh, can you dump /proc/vmstat and a small allocator histogram?

chen: pasted quick sample from the failing host (nvlink, A100):
```
pgpgin 1234567
pgpgout 89012
pgfault 345678
slab_reclaim 3456
kv_compact_ops 12
kv_frag_pct 38
```
Not great. Also noticed `kv.compact_quantum` is 0.1 on Dedicated, 0.25 on Hosted.

diego: interesting — compact_quantum was tuned lower for latency on Dedicated. Might be the tradeoff: less compaction => more free fragment accumulation then big paging bursts. :thinking:

sam: can we repro on a small Dedicated replica with perf events? I can spin one up.

maria: also check VPC path MTU and NIC offloads on Dedicated vs Hosted; we had subtle pacing differences before that changed batching window.

ops-bot: Deploy started by sam: kv-repro-smallpool (id: repro-47). Logs will stream to /var/log/kv-repro-47.log

chen: repro shows repeated small evict/rehydrate cycles — latency OK but cumulative resident set grows until a big pageback that stalls the workload for ~700ms.

perf-bot: perf report (top hotspots):
```
- kv_reclaim_slab: 24%
- kv_page_walk: 18%
- memcpy: 12%
- kernel_copy: 8%
```

alice: that reclaim slab hotspot + page_walk suggests fragmentation pressure, not a pure leak. Two knobs to try: increase compact_quantum to 0.3 on Dedicated; and enable `kv.prefetch_bounded=true` to avoid immediate rehydration thrash.

diego: agree. Also try raising `kv.compact_window_ms` from 50 -> 120 and measure latency tail. Might batch compaction better across long contexts.

sam: I'm going to flip compact_quantum on repro host and run 12h overnight. Will capture pmap + perf every hour.

maria: note that Private (on-prem) runs with older kernel 5.15 and had `zone_reclaim` enabled in sysctl for memory locality. That interacts with our compaction latency. If we change compact policy, we should test on Private before rolling.

chen: good call. I also ran a quick comparison: Hosted (GKE) with compact_quantum=0.25 and prefetch disabled showed stable RSS over 72h. Dedicated with 0.1 drifted. Private with 0.25 and zone_reclaim=1 also drifted but via different pattern (NUMA-local pages held, very localized fragmentation).

alice: plan: 1) sam runs the overnight test with compact_quantum=0.3 + prefetch_bounded=true on Dedicated repro. 2) diego will run a Private repro with same config but kernel 5.15 and zone_reclaim=1. 3) if both stable, stage change to canary Dedicated pool. 4) monitor perf-bot regression alerts for latency tail.

diego: I'll also snapshot jemalloc stats and post a small script to correlate slab run lengths with sequence lengths. Might expose a pattern where certain long-context seqs allocate lots of small frames that defeat coalescing.

sam: started the job: repro-47 now running with new knobs. Will share logs in thread as we get hourly dumps. :rocket:

chen: thanks. Also adding a short note for console: we should show `kv.compact_quantum` per-deployment in the Console so customers see config drift between Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Small ops confusion already.

maria: agreed — add to roadmap item for infra-config UI.

alice: nice troubleshooting, team. If the overnight runs are green we should document the new defaults and the reasoning in eng-runtime runbook.

chen: adding runbook PR after we confirm. Keeping thread open for logs.
